title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a list of equivalent descriptions of a 'projective connection' (projective structure) on a smooth relative curve X/S. The previous page gives the other descriptions:
(a) a P^1-bundle P with a connection relative to S and a section σ that is nowhere horizontal. In modern terms this is a PGL2-oper, or an indigenous bundle.
(b) an sl2-type Lie algebra bundle with a filtration and a connection satisfying a transversality condition. This is the Lie-algebra form of an oper; the bundle is built from Sym^2 of the first jet bundle P^1(ω).
(c) an extension of the canonical isomorphism O_P/J^3 ≅ P^2_{X/S} to order 3, i.e. a third-order 'osculating' datum.
(d) a third-order differential equation on P^1_X invariant under PGL2. This is the Schwarzian equation S(f)=q.

This page adds (e), for S = Spec C and X compact: a subsheaf U of the sheaf of analytic maps X^an → P^1(C). It must consist of local isomorphisms (local charts) and be a left torsor under the constant sheaf PGL(2,C). This is a classical complex projective structure, an atlas with Möbius transition maps.

The page then proves the equivalences.
- (d)⇒(e). Take the sheaf of germs of local solutions of the invariant third-order ODE. Any two local solutions differ by a unique element of PGL2(C), so the solutions form a torsor.
- (e)⇒(a).
  - Turn the left torsor into a right torsor by inversion and form the associated P^1-bundle P^an = U ×^{PGL2} P^1. It carries a flat analytic connection, coming from the constant structure group.
  - A point of P^an over x is a class of pairs (f,y), with f a germ in U_x and y in P^1(C), under the relation (f,y) ~ (σ∘f, σ(y)).
  - All pairs (f, f(x)) are equivalent. This gives a canonical point of each fibre, hence a section of P^an. This is the developing-map section.
  - Trivialising P|U by a chart f identifies this section with f itself. So the section is analytic, and it is nowhere horizontal because f is a local isomorphism.
  - GAGA, using compactness of X, algebraises (P, connection, σ).
- (a)⇒(e). Begun at the bottom of the page and finished on the next. Use the flat connection to trivialise P^an|U ≅ U × P_x for small U. The nowhere-horizontal section then becomes a local biholomorphism U → P^1(C), and these germs form the torsor U.

The overall purpose is to set up projective connections on relative curves in several equivalent algebraic forms. The surrounding dossier suggests this is meant for relative or characteristic-p settings (Gauss–Manin connection, Cartier operation). The analytic dictionary on this page serves as the motivating model.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor gap: in (e)⇒(a), compactness is needed only for the final GAGA step (algebraising the bundle, connection and section), and this is stated only implicitly.

In (d)⇒(e) the claim that local solutions are PGL2-conjugate assumes solutions are taken to be local isomorphisms (non-degenerate solutions of the Schwarzian equation). Condition (d) on the previous page ('isomorphismes locaux d'ordre 3') covers this.

ideas.what: Complex projective structure on a Riemann surface as a PGL2(C)-torsor of local charts (sheaf of germs of local isomorphisms to P^1)
Equivalence of projective structures with flat P^1-bundles carrying a nowhere-horizontal section, via the developing-map section and GAGA
Local solutions of a PGL2-invariant third-order ODE form a PGL2-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian equation; projective structures from quadratic differentials

missed.claim: The page belongs to a relative, algebraic treatment of projective connections on curves over a general base S. It sits next to notes on the Cartier operation and Gauss–Manin connections, and uses formulations (a), (a′) and (c) via jet bundles P^n_{X/S}. This anticipates the relative indigenous-bundle and oper formalism later used in characteristic p (Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory, dormant opers). The analytic case on this page is only the motivating dictionary; any char-p content would have to be checked on other pages.
missed.quote: On passe de e) à a) en considérant le torseur à gauche ... prenant le fibré projectif associé ... une section de P^an sur X^an ... analytique et nulle part horizontale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early (c. 1972?) relative, scheme-theoretic definition of opers as (P,σ,c) with σ nowhere horizontal, predating Beilinson–Drinfeld. It is of historical interest for the genealogy of opers and indigenous bundles.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is the classical equivalence between projective structures, Schwarzian equations and indigenous bundles, done carefully. The only point of interest is historical: Grothendieck's relative oper-like formulation appears in a dossier also concerned with Cartier operations.
